title: Sign of price minus a 2-10 month average, daily, on gold, silver, oil, FX majors and S&P 500
source: Lemperiere, Deremble, Seager, Potters & Bouchaud (2014), Two centuries of trend following, arXiv:1404.3274 (eq. 1-2, Table 1)
why: Paper: signal s_n = (p - EWMA_n(p)) / sigma_n, position = sign(s_n), Sharpe 0.65-0.83 for n = 2-15 months (Table 1). The engine has no EWMA, so the nearest is a simple MA: fast 1 (price) against slow 42, 105 and 210 trading days (about 2, 5 and 10 months). Approximations: simple MA not EWMA, no volatility scaling (sign only, so sigma does not matter here), daily not monthly, and the paper's pool is futures on many markets; its FX result since 1973 is Sharpe 0.57. Each variant is a DSR trial.
